title: Unique Playlist
statement:
A radio station's playlist is written as a string: every letter is one song, and equal letters mean the same song. A listener hates hearing a song twice, so they want to tune in for a **contiguous** part of the playlist in which every song is different.

Find the length of the longest substring of **s** that has no repeated letters.
input: One line with the string **s** of lowercase English letters.
output: Print one integer: the length of the longest substring without repeated letters.

samples.explanation: `abc` is a longest part without repeats.
`wke` works. Note that `pwke` is not contiguous, so it does not count.

hints: Use a sliding window [left, i]. Move i to the right one letter at a time.
Remember the last position of every letter. If the current letter was last seen inside the window, move left just past that position.
editorial:
Keep a window `[left, i]` that contains no repeated letter and an array `last[c]` with the last index where letter c appeared. When you add `s[i]`, if `last[s[i]] ≥ left`, the letter is already in the window, so set `left = last[s[i]] + 1`. Update `last[s[i]] = i` and the answer with `i - left + 1`. Both ends only move to the right.

Complexity: O(n).
